title: Document a response attempt
summary: Record who was contacted, when, whether anyone replied, and what assistance actually followed.
requirements: Protect personal details and precise animal locations
Use the responsible official or rescue contact for urgent concerns
availability_status: Documentation activity available; no Crossover submission form
why_it_helps: An attempted contact, a reply, and actual assistance are separate results. Recording each reveals where a response may stall.
what_to_expect: Note the report date, general area, contact route, reply, and any observed care or unresolved need.
Keep private details out of public notes. A reply alone does not prove the need was resolved.

title: Verify a dog-care service
summary: Check a responder's current scope, eligibility, contact route, and conditions for participation.
availability_status: Verification activity available; specific opportunities remain unconfirmed
why_it_helps: A published service description does not establish current capacity or the outcome of a particular request.
what_to_expect: Compare a public service description with a dated, direct answer from Stockton Animal Services or a rescue organization.
Record unanswered questions and avoid inferring that an unverified service is ineffective.

title: Identify a missing care capability
summary: Document a specific unmet need after checking what existing responders can provide.
availability_status: Investigation available; need and proposed response require evidence
why_it_helps: A confirmed gap can guide a safe, specific response without assuming that a service failed simply because its outcome is unknown.
what_to_expect: Describe the general need, sources checked, responses received, and what remains unresolved.
Do not organize animal custody, transport, or placement without the responsible parties and applicable requirements.

title: Check a reported stray-dog area
summary: Visit a previously reported area from a safe public location, observe current conditions, and document findings.
requirements: Follow the investigation's safety, privacy, and field observation guidance
availability_status: Observation activity available; specific visits are planned separately
why_it_helps: A short, documented visit can distinguish a past report from current conditions and identify what remains uncertain.
what_to_expect: Choose a previously reported general area using the dogs investigation and its field observation procedure.
Observe from a safe public location. Do not approach, pursue, or handle dogs.
Record the visit date, approximate period, what you saw and did not see, possible care or distress, and follow-up needed. Protect precise locations and personal privacy.
A single visit, including one with no dogs observed, does not establish conditions across a neighborhood.

title: Report a stray dog
summary: Record the date, general location, description, and safety concerns, then contact the appropriate official service or lost-and-found channel.
requirements: Have the sighting date, general location, description, and safety concerns ready
availability_status: Official online complaint and phone contact available; response depends on circumstances

at_a_glance.why: Gets a current report to the right service

why_it_helps: A dated report can help the responsible service assess an animal's welfare and public safety without treating an unverified sighting as a confirmed rescue need.
what_to_expect: Observing means recording what you actually see from a safe distance; it does not establish that the dog is abandoned or needs custody.
Reporting means using the City's animal complaint page and selecting Animals → Animals - other, or calling Stockton Animal Services at (209) 937-7445. Call for an injured, sick, or aggressive animal.
For an incident in an unincorporated part of San Joaquin County, the City directs residents to County Animal Control at (209) 953-6070.
Taking custody is a separate step. If you have found a dog and want to bring it to the shelter, call (209) 937-7445 during business hours to schedule a drop-off appointment.
For after-hours emergencies, the City lists Stockton Police dispatch at (209) 937-8377. For an animal attack in progress, call 911.

title: Help feed street dogs
summary: Investigate existing food and water assistance, useful supplies, and safe ways residents may be able to participate.
requirements: Confirm needs and instructions with responders before supplying or feeding
Do not start independent routes or approach unfamiliar dogs
evidence_label: CBS Sacramento: Stockton Streetdogs feeding work, April 6, 2026
availability_status: Care coordination under investigation; participation instructions not yet verified

at_a_glance.why: Makes useful help easier to identify

why_it_helps: Stockton Streetdogs' feeding operation is documented, but Crossover has not established public participation instructions, supply needs, or safe volunteer roles.
what_to_expect: Review the investigation's Community Care Coordination questions and the published account of Stockton Streetdogs' feeding work.
Ask responders what food and water support already operates, what supplies are useful, and whether residents can safely join established work.
Independent feeding sites, new routes, and volunteer assignments are not currently verified opportunities.

title: Foster a dog
summary: Open your home temporarily to a dog that needs safe placement.
why_it_helps: Opening your home gives a dog a safe place to land while rescue partners work toward longer-term placement. Each foster can also create room for another dog to be helped.
what_to_expect: You’ll leave Crossover to view Stockton Street Dogs’ current foster information and contact options.
The length and needs of a foster placement can vary by dog.
The provider can walk you through current needs and next steps.

title: Transport a dog
summary: Help move a dog to veterinary care, foster placement, or another safe destination.
why_it_helps: Transportation can be the missing link between a dog and veterinary care, foster placement, rescue transfer, or another safe destination.
what_to_expect: Transport needs depend on current rescue activity and may not be available at all times.
Confirm the destination, timing, and any handling instructions before committing.
This action is currently marked unverified in Crossover, so check directly with the provider.

title: Take a shelter dog out
summary: Sign up to give a Stockton shelter dog a break from shelter life through a walk, car ride, or quality time with a caring person.
why_it_helps: A few hours outside the shelter can reduce stress, create community visibility, and help a dog connect with potential fosters or adopters.
handoff_label: Sign up with Stockton Animal Services

at_a_glance.why: Gives dogs a break and community exposure

what_to_expect: Sign up through the City of Stockton Animal Services volunteer page.
Volunteers must be 16 or older; ages 16–17 need written parent or guardian approval.
Attend a brief orientation before choosing a dog.
Take your dog on a walk, car ride, or quality-time outing, then return them to the shelter.
For questions, email SASVolunteers@stocktonca.gov or call (209) 937-7445 during normal business hours.
